title: Care Management Hold Maximums and Postpartum Closure Period
content:
Two Care Management figures are counted in calendar days and bound how long an episode lasts in particular circumstances: the most calendar days an enrollment may stay on hold, and, for maternal care, the calendar days after the pregnancy end date on which the episode closes.

| Care Management tier | Most calendar days on hold | Maternal closure: calendar days after the pregnancy end date |
|---|---|---|
| Healthy Living Support | 0 | 0 |
| Care Coordination Level 1 | 60 | 0 |
| Care Coordination Level 2 | 60 | 0 |
| Maternal Care Management | 30 | 365 |
| Complex Case Management | 90 | 0 |
| Health Home Services | 90 | 0 |
| LTSS Service Coordination | 60 | 0 |

## Reading the table

- **Hold maximum**: the most calendar days an enrollment may stay on hold in the tier. Complex Case Management and Health Home Services allow the longest hold, 90 calendar days; Maternal Care Management the shortest of the tiers with a hold figure above 0, 30 calendar days.
- **Maternal closure period**: applies to Maternal Care Management only, where the figure is 365 calendar days after the pregnancy end date. A 0 in this column means the figure does not apply to the tier.

## Hypothetical example

A hypothetical Maternal Care Management member whose pregnancy ended on 15 August 2025 reaches 365 calendar days after that date on 15 August 2026, the day on which the maternal episode closes. The same member, if placed on hold, has a hold maximum of 30 calendar days, against 90 for a member of Health Home Services.
